Rocuronium is not eliminated by organ-independent Hofmann degradation; it depends mainly on hepatobiliary excretion.
Plain lidocaine maximum is about 3 mg/kg (some quote 4.5 mg/kg); with adrenaline it rises to 7 mg/kg.
Adrenaline slows systemic absorption, raising the lidocaine maximum to 7 mg/kg.
Prilocaine has the least systemic toxicity of the amide local anaesthetics, but in large doses it causes methaemoglobinaemia.
Prilocaine is metabolised to o-toluidine, which oxidises haemoglobin and causes methaemoglobinaemia.
Bupivacaine binds cardiac sodium channels tightly and causes refractory arrhythmias and cardiac arrest, so it is contraindicated for IV regional anaesthesia.
Ropivacaine has greater sensory-motor separation and less cardiotoxicity than bupivacaine; levobupivacaine is less cardiotoxic but separation is the ropivacaine hallmark.
Bupivacaine is long-acting, has a maximum dose of about 2 mg/kg, is never given IV and is more cardiotoxic than ropivacaine.
Levobupivacaine is the S-enantiomer of bupivacaine and is less cardiotoxic.
Ropivacaine's greater sensory-motor differentiation gives labour analgesia with less motor block.
Prilocaine has the least systemic toxicity and is not more cardiotoxic than bupivacaine; its typical adverse effect is methaemoglobinaemia.
Methoxyflurane metabolism releases inorganic fluoride, causing high-output renal failure.
Oxidative metabolism of halothane forms trifluoroacetylated proteins that trigger immune hepatitis, limiting its use.
Methoxyflurane is nephrotoxic and halothane hepatotoxic, so statements 3 and 4 are correct.
Isoflurane undergoes minimal metabolism and is a suitable volatile agent after halothane hepatitis; nitrous oxide is too weak to use alone.
Ketamine is a phencyclidine derivative that keeps airway reflexes and respiratory drive.
Prilocaine maximum is about 6 mg/kg plain and roughly 8-9 mg/kg with adrenaline; 9 mg/kg is the closest option.
Ropivacaine is less cardiotoxic than bupivacaine, so statement 3 is wrong; the other statements are correct.
Sugammadex encapsulates steroidal non-depolarising blockers (rocuronium, vecuronium); succinylcholine is ended by plasma cholinesterase.
Propofol suits infusion, etomidate is cardiostable but suppresses adrenal steroidogenesis, ketamine causes emergence delirium; thiopentone lowers ICP.
Thiopentone reduces cerebral metabolic rate, cerebral blood flow and ICP, which is why it suits neuroanaesthesia.
Thiopentone is a thiobarbiturate; propofol is a phenol, etomidate an imidazole and ketamine a phencyclidine derivative.
Ketamine's sympathomimetic action maintains blood pressure and it gives analgesia with preserved airway reflexes, ideal for hypovolaemic trauma.
RSI secures the airway in aspiration-risk and emergency patients using IV induction plus a rapid-onset relaxant, not inhalational agent with opioid.
The E suffix marks emergency surgery and leaves the physical status grade unchanged, so ASA III becomes ASA IIIE.
Bupivacaine's longer action comes mainly from its higher protein binding (and lipid solubility) compared with lidocaine.
POSSUM scores 12 physiological and 6 operative severity variables to predict postoperative mortality and morbidity.
Class 1 is easiest and class 4 shows only hard palate; class 2 shows fauces and part of uvula and class 3 soft palate only, so statements 2 and 3 are wrong.
Ropivacaine maximum dose is usually quoted as about 3 mg/kg (3-4 mg/kg), higher than bupivacaine's 2 mg/kg.
Symptomatic heart failure with ischaemic heart disease is severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life (ASA IV), and the emergency makes it IVE.
Vecuronium is cleared hepatically and renally, not by Hofmann degradation; the other three pairings are correct.
Thiopentone lowers intracranial pressure; the other statements are correct.
Lidocaine has a rapid onset, intermediate-to-short duration and a good sensory block.
High-dose rocuronium gives intubating conditions in about 60 s and sugammadex allows rapid reversal, making it a valid RSI alternative.
A healthy patient with no systemic disease is ASA I (with E suffix if the surgery is an emergency).
ASA is a physical status classification, POSSUM can be scored postoperatively and ACS NSQIP is a risk calculator; Mallampati is an airway test, not a mortality score.
Ketamine, a dissociative NMDA antagonist, characteristically causes emergence delirium with vivid dreams and hallucinations.
FEV1 is a pulmonary function test, not a bedside airway assessment parameter like Mallampati, thyromental distance or jaw protrusion.
Etomidate causes minimal myocardial depression and vasodilatation, which is why it is chosen for haemodynamically unstable patients.
Head extension at the atlanto-occipital joint is assessed to judge alignment of airway axes for laryngoscopy.
Bupivacaine has a maximum dose of about 2 mg/kg and is contraindicated IV because of cardiotoxicity.
Bupivacaine is long acting but highly cardiotoxic and must never be given intravenously, e.g. for IV regional block.
ASA IV is severe disease that is a constant threat to life, and ASA V is a moribund patient, so statements 3 and 4 are swapped.
Bupivacaine's maximum dose is about 2 mg/kg, not 3; the commonly quoted lidocaine 3 mg/kg, prilocaine 6 mg/kg and ropivacaine 3 mg/kg are accepted.
Etomidate inhibits adrenal 11-beta-hydroxylase, so repeated doses or infusions cause adrenocortical suppression.
Etomidate inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase and suppresses adrenal cortisol synthesis.
Vecuronium is deacetylated in the liver and excreted in bile, so hepatic impairment prolongs its effect.
POSSUM predicts postoperative mortality and morbidity.
The Bromage scale grades motor block after neuraxial anaesthesia; POSSUM, ASA and ACS NSQIP are risk assessment tools.
Atracurium is preferred, not avoided, in renal and hepatic failure; the other statements are correct.
Thiopentone is a thiobarbiturate IV induction agent.
Levobupivacaine is the S-enantiomer of bupivacaine, with similar duration and less cardiotoxicity.

Propofol suits TIVA because it does not accumulate and allows infusion with smooth recovery, but it causes more hypotension than thiopentone, so the 'better haemodynamic stability' part of R is doubtful.
Thiopentone reduces cerebral metabolic rate and lowers intracranial pressure; the other pairings are correct.
NSQIP is the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program of the American College of Surgeons, which provides a perioperative risk calculator.
Ropivacaine produces less motor block than bupivacaine; prilocaine is the least toxic and levobupivacaine less cardiotoxic, so 2 and 4 are correct.
Levobupivacaine is chosen over racemic bupivacaine because, as its S-isomer, it is less cardiotoxic.
Methoxyflurane is nephrotoxic via fluoride and halothane is hepatotoxic; halothane is not nephrotoxic and isoflurane is not meaningfully hepatotoxic.
Atracurium's Hofmann elimination is independent of renal function.
Propofol is an alkyl phenol, not a steroid; ketamine is a phencyclidine derivative, etomidate is short acting and thiopentone depresses the myocardium.
Mandibular protrusion is tested directly by asking the patient to protrude the jaw (upper lip bite test).
Thiopentone is a barbiturate and etomidate is grouped as a steroid-like (imidazole) agent; propofol is the phenol and ketamine the phencyclidine, so 3 and 4 are reversed.
Suxamethonium depolarisation releases potassium, and after burns or denervation, upregulated extrajunctional receptors exaggerate this into dangerous hyperkalaemia.
Recent MI with severe COPD and uncontrolled diabetes is severe systemic disease that threatens life, ASA IV, with E added for emergency surgery.
Succinylcholine triggers malignant hyperthermia and is contraindicated in susceptible patients; it has the fastest onset and short action, and pseudocholinesterase deficiency causes prolonged apnoea.
The first-trimester combined test is free beta-hCG, PAPP-A and nuchal translucency; AFP belongs to second-trimester screening.
Wernicke encephalopathy in hyperemesis gravidarum is caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.
The modified biophysical profile is an NST plus amniotic fluid index, not fetal breathing.
Physiological oedema of pregnancy is mild ankle oedema that disappears with rest and has no cardiac or renal cause.
Compared with mature milk, colostrum has more protein, vitamin A, sodium and immunoglobulin, and less fat and lactose.
Pre-conception counselling is preventive care recommended for all women planning pregnancy, not only those with complications.
A reactive NST means a healthy fetus, but the NST false-negative rate is about 0.5% and 50% is its false-positive rate, so statement 3 is wrong as printed.
Antenatal care increases institutional deliveries and reduces maternal and perinatal mortality and morbidity.
Excess hCG, estrogen and progesterone are the proposed hormonal causes of hyperemesis gravidarum; hPL is not.
In Down syndrome, hCG and inhibin A are raised while AFP and unconjugated estriol are low, so only statement 1 is correct.
Ultrasound is operator-dependent with a long learning curve; it is radiation-free, cheap and allows dynamic studies.
Statement IV mislabels the phases: anagen is growth, catagen transitional and telogen resting; the other statements are correct.
An ulcer is a secondary lesion that develops from loss of tissue; patch, vesicle and wheal are primary lesions.
Malassezia in pityriasis versicolor appears as short hyphae and round yeasts on KOH mount, the spaghetti-and-meatballs pattern.
Perioral grouped vesicles with multinucleated giant cells on Tzanck smear indicate herpes simplex (labialis).
Apple-jelly nodules on diascopy are classic for lupus vulgaris (cutaneous tuberculosis), though granulomas such as sarcoidosis can look similar.
Under Wood's lamp Pseudomonas glows yellow-green to pale blue-green and vitiligo shows bright blue-white accentuation, so 'pale blue' could fit either.
The ABCDE melanoma criteria are Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Colour variation, Diameter over 6 mm and Evolution.
Asteatotic eczema (eczema craquele, winter itch) is also called xerotic eczema, arising on very dry skin.
Itching with cracked, crazy-paving dry skin over the shins of an elderly person in winter is asteatotic eczema.
Itchy flexural eczema with lichenification, Dennie-Morgan infraorbital folds and nails polished by scratching indicate atopic dermatitis.
Wickham striae, fine white lines on violaceous papules, are characteristic of lichen planus.
A painless genital chancre a month before a generalised maculopapular rash points to secondary syphilis.
Midline defects such as cleft palate go with hypothalamic-pituitary maldevelopment, so polyuria suggests central DI from hypopituitarism.
A marked rise in urine osmolality after desmopressin, following failed concentration on water deprivation, confirms central DI.
Polyuria in children is defined as urine output above 2 L/m2/day.
In central DI, water deprivation fails to concentrate the urine while serum sodium and osmolality rise, and urine osmolality rises after vasopressin.
Lissencephaly is a neuronal migration defect in which gyri fail to form, leaving a smooth brain.
Centrotemporal (Rolandic) spikes are seen in benign Rolandic epilepsy; SSPE shows periodic complexes, so IV is wrong.
Ethosuximide or valproate, not lamotrigine, is first choice for absence seizures; the other pairings are standard.
Generalised 3 Hz spike-and-wave discharges provoked by hyperventilation are diagnostic of childhood absence epilepsy.
Oxcarbazepine (or carbamazepine) is first-line for focal seizures in children.
Raised ICP is managed with head elevation to 30 degrees in midline, brief hyperventilation to PaCO2 30-35 and mannitol; hypertonic, not hypotonic, saline is used.
Grey matter degenerations present with early seizures, cognitive decline and retinal changes; peripheral neuropathy and spasticity suggest white matter disease.
Demyelination prolongs distal latency, markedly slows conduction velocity and causes conduction block; 'increased velocity' as printed is wrong, so no option fits.
The HLH-2004 criteria include fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hypertriglyceridaemia or hypofibrinogenaemia and ferritin of 500 or more.
Childhood Takayasu criteria need angiographic abnormality plus one of: pulse deficit or claudication, limb BP difference over 10 mmHg, bruits, hypertension or raised acute phase reactants.
Hand-foot-and-mouth disease is classically caused by coxsackievirus A16 (and enterovirus 71).
In cryptophthalmos, skin continuous over the orbit and fused lids completely cover the globe.
Preterm birth complications are the leading cause of neonatal deaths in India.
Birth before 37 completed weeks is preterm; at 2.6 kg the baby is not low birth weight (under 2.5 kg).
Perinatal mortality is late fetal deaths (stillbirths) plus early neonatal deaths within the first week, per 1000 live births.
In primary apnoea, breathing stops and heart rate falls but blood pressure is maintained, and stimulation can restart breathing.
Apnoea not responding to stimulation, with bradycardia, flaccidity and falling BP, is secondary apnoea and needs positive pressure ventilation.
Each of the five APGAR signs scores 0 when absent, giving a total of 0.
APGAR has five signs scored 0-2 each, so the maximum is 10.
Persistent apnoea or gasping after the initial steps calls for positive pressure ventilation within the golden minute.
Preterm resuscitation starts with 21-30% oxygen, titrated to target saturations.
Bag and mask ventilation is contraindicated in suspected congenital diaphragmatic hernia because it inflates the herniated bowel; intubate instead.
Neonatal CPR uses a 3:1 ratio, giving 90 compressions and 30 breaths (120 events) per minute.
NBSUs at FRUs/CHCs stabilise sick newborns and manage low birth weight babies above 1800 g; smaller babies go to an SNCU.
Weighing after skin-to-skin contact, full examination and breastfeeding within 1 hour are correct; rooming-in is encouraged, not avoided.
Vitamin K1 is 0.5 mg IM for babies under 1000 g and 1 mg IM above 1000 g; option C has lost the '<' and the second half but is the intended answer.
Discharge requires immunisation given, no significant jaundice or illness and a confident mother; the birth Apgar score is not a discharge criterion.
Corticosteroids, hormonal contraceptives and beta-blockers can cause weight gain; ACE inhibitors are weight-neutral.
A fasting plasma glucose of 7.0 mmol/L or more in pregnancy indicates overt diabetes, not gestational diabetes; GDM uses fasting 5.1-6.9, 1-hour >=10.0 and 2-hour 8.5-11.0 mmol/L.
Since the 2017 revision, blindness under NPCBVI is presenting visual acuity worse than 3/60 in the better eye.
Near vision impairment is defined as presenting near visual acuity worse than N6 (M0.8) at 40 cm with existing correction.
Koplik spots, bluish-white spots on a red base opposite the lower molars, are pathognomonic of measles.
WHO advises MCV1 at 9 months where transmission is high, and at 12 months where measles transmission is low.
Chickenpox rash is centripetal, densest on the trunk, affects flexor more than extensor surfaces, and usually spares palms and soles.
Monkeypox is an enveloped double-stranded DNA orthopoxvirus of the Poxviridae family, with a usual incubation period of 6-13 days.
The standard adult treatment dose of oseltamivir is 75 mg orally twice daily for 5 days.
The classic Gregg triad of congenital rubella is cataract, sensorineural deafness and cardiac defects such as PDA.
GAPPD 2025 goals: pneumonia deaths <3 and diarrhoea deaths <1 per 1000 live births, 75% less severe pneumonia and diarrhoea, and 40% less stunting.
Mumps is caused by an RNA paramyxovirus, so statement 4 is false. It is most infectious just before parotitis, and orchitis is the commonest extra-salivary feature in adults.
The End TB 2030 milestone is an 80% fall in incidence from 2015, about <20 per 100,000. The <10 per 100,000 figure is the 2035 target.
A scatter diagram plots paired values of two variables and shows whether they are correlated.
The standard normal curve is bell-shaped and symmetrical with mean 0, SD 1 and total area 1, not 2.
The eight values sum to 664, and 664/8 = 83 mmHg.
Range is the highest value minus the lowest value: 48 - 22 = 26 years.
The planning cycle starts with analysing the health situation (gathering and analysing data, formulating problems), then sets priorities before implementation and evaluation.
An objective is precise, a planned endpoint and directly concerned with the problem, but it is constrained by time, so statement 4 is false.
Models are a quantitative management method. MBO, information systems and communication are methods based on behavioural sciences.
Work sampling measures how staff time is used, which helps standardise job methods and work out manpower needs.
The elements of evaluation are relevance, adequacy, accessibility, acceptability, effectiveness, efficiency and impact. Availability is not one of them.
Parkinson disease causes reduced blinking, drooling and hypophonia. Handwriting becomes small (micrographia), not large.
A long-term vegan with paraesthesiae and sensory ataxia suggests subacute combined degeneration from vitamin B12 deficiency.
Sleep deprivation, missed antiepileptic doses, recreational drugs and physical exhaustion are all recognised seizure triggers.
Hypothyroidism, B12 deficiency and thiamine deficiency cause treatable cognitive decline. Lewy body dementia is an irreversible neurodegenerative disease.
Frontotemporal dementia causes personality and language change with relatively spared early memory. Cholinesterase inhibitors do not help it.
About 85% of non-traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhages come from rupture of a saccular (berry) aneurysm.
The glymphatic system is a glia-dependent perivascular CSF pathway that clears waste from the brain, mainly during sleep.
Parkinsonism typically shows hypomimia, hypophonic dysphonia, festinating gait and cogwheel rigidity.
In transient global amnesia, consciousness and complex motor function are preserved, so statement 3 is false. The other three statements are correct.
Cluster headache gives periodic, strictly unilateral periorbital pain lasting 15-180 minutes with ipsilateral autonomic features, aborted by subcutaneous sumatriptan or 100% oxygen.
Flickering lights, recreational drugs, poor antiepileptic adherence and sleep deprivation are all recognised seizure triggers.
Familial Alzheimer disease, Huntington disease and Wilson disease are inherited causes of dementia. Punch-drunk syndrome results from repeated head trauma.
Focal motor seizures may show a Jacksonian march, postictal Todd paralysis, or continuous focal activity (epilepsia partialis continua).
Recent head injury, recent MI and GI bleeding within 21 days are contraindications to thrombolysis. The blood pressure cut-off is above 185/110 mmHg, not 150/100.
Post-LP headache is a dull occipitofrontal headache that eases on lying down. It is mildest on waking after lying overnight and worsens through the day when upright.
Essential tremor can start at any age and often eases with a little alcohol. The head and voice are often involved, so statement 2 is false.
Antipsychotics (including some atypical agents such as risperidone) and lithium can cause drug-induced parkinsonism, and MPTP destroys nigral dopaminergic neurons.
Lead-pipe and cogwheel rigidity and a festinating gait are parkinsonian. A positive Romberg test indicates sensory (proprioceptive) ataxia.
Idiopathic PD typically begins asymmetrically, so statement 1 is false. Hyposmia, constipation, early preserved cognition and hypophonic speech are typical.
Levodopa works best on bradykinesia and rigidity rather than tremor. Little of it reaches the brain, domperidone offsets nausea, and it can cause hallucinations.
Sickle cell disease, smoking and atrial fibrillation are stroke risk factors. Raised fibrinogen raises stroke risk, not hypofibrinogenaemia.
Myasthenia gravis targets postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors, so statement 3 is false. Fatigable weakness worse by evening, bulbar symptoms and penicillamine-induced disease are typical.
TB meningitis is paucibacillary, so CSF smears are often negative. Culture is the reference standard, and Xpert MTB/RIF (Ultra) is recommended as the initial CSF test.
Night paraesthesia and weak thumb abduction are typical and hypothenar wasting is ulnar; palm sensation is often spared via the palmar cutaneous branch, but A is the best code.
Tetracyclines, retinoids and excess vitamin A are the classic drug causes of idiopathic intracranial hypertension. Sulfonamides are not a standard association.
HIV, alcohol and phenytoin cause polyneuropathy. Among antituberculous drugs it is isoniazid that causes neuropathy, not rifampicin.
ICH is about 10-15% of strokes, and hypertensive ICH is mainly deep (putamen, thalamus), so statements 1 and 2 are false. Statements 3 and 4 are correct.
A dominant parietal lesion causes dysphasia, acalculia and dyslexia (Gerstmann features). Contralateral neglect is typical of a non-dominant parietal lesion.
NF1 shows axillary freckling and neurofibromas. Cutaneous schwannomas belong to NF2, which leaves option B.
Parkinson disease gives bradykinesia, rigidity and a mask-like face. A spastic gait is pyramidal and not a feature.
A wide-based, shuffling gait with freezing and trouble starting and turning, but a normal heel-shin test, is a frontal (higher-level) gait disorder.
The Cushing triad is hypertension, bradycardia and irregular respiration. Hypothermia is not part of it.
Post-LP headache is postural: it begins within 48 hours, worsens on sitting, eases with caffeine, and is least severe on waking after lying down.
Huntington disease, Alzheimer disease and thiamine deficiency cause dementia. Vitamin D toxicity is not a recognised cause.
Slight painless bleeding with a closed os, a uterus matching dates and fetal cardiac activity is a threatened miscarriage.
An abortion is considered septic when temperature is 38 C (100.4 F) or more for at least 24 hours, with other signs of pelvic infection.
Poorly controlled diabetes, antiphospholipid syndrome and hyperhomocysteinaemia are accepted causes. Endometriosis appears in some lists, so the key accepts all four.
Passing grape-like vesicles, a uterus larger than dates and no fetal heart point to a complete hydatidiform mole.
Traditionally pregnancy is avoided for one year after molar evacuation. Newer advice allows it about 6 months after hCG becomes normal.
Frozen shoulder shows global restriction with loss of external rotation (active and passive) as the hallmark, with normal radiographs.
De Quervain disease is stenosing tenosynovitis of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis in the first dorsal compartment.
Morton neuroma most often affects the third web space, less often the second.
Ewing sarcoma typically carries t(11;22), producing the EWS-FLI1 fusion gene.
Kienbock disease is avascular necrosis of the lunate; Preiser disease affects the scaphoid.
Scoliosis is defined as a coronal Cobb angle of 10 degrees or more.
Perthes disease is avascular necrosis of the femoral head, typically in boys aged 4-8 years.
Ponseti casting first corrects forefoot cavus by supinating the forefoot and lifting the first ray, then adductus and varus, and equinus last.
Osteoid osteoma is a cortical lesion with a small central nidus and dense sclerosis, most often in the proximal femur and tibia.
Morton neuroma is managed first with footwear change and guided steroid injection. Excision is kept for failures because of the risk of a painful stump neuroma.
Eosinophilic granuloma of a vertebral body classically causes uniform collapse, vertebra plana.
Ulnar nerve palsy wastes the hypothenar muscles and interossei while sparing the thenar eminence. The root labels in the stem and explanation are imprecise.
In Froment sign, the patient flexes the thumb IP joint (FPL, median nerve) to make up for a weak adductor pollicis supplied by the ulnar nerve.
Thenar wasting reflects established motor axon loss and is a late sign of carpal tunnel syndrome.
Lumbar canal stenosis narrows further in extension, so symptoms come on with standing and walking and ease with flexion.
In the Ponseti method, residual hindfoot equinus is corrected by percutaneous Achilles tenotomy before the final cast.
Parosteal osteosarcoma is a low-grade surface tumour, classically of the posterior distal femur, with a long, mildly symptomatic course.
Tennis elbow is tendinosis at the common extensor origin on the lateral epicondyle.
Kohler disease is osteochondrosis (AVN) of the tarsal navicular. Kienbock affects the lunate, Panner the capitellum and Freiberg the second metatarsal head.
In Perthes disease, revascularisation of the necrotic femoral head starts the fragmentation (resorption) and reossification stages.
Soft-tissue lumps that are large (over 5 cm), deep to the fascia, painful, enlarging or recurrent are suspicious. A superficial location is not a warning sign.
The Ottawa ankle rules use bone tenderness along the posterior edge of the distal 6 cm or the tip of either malleolus, or inability to bear weight.
In Langerhans cell histiocytosis, the unifocal form is eosinophilic granuloma, the multifocal form Hand-Schuller-Christian, and the disseminated form Letterer-Siwe disease.
Dupuytren contracture mostly affects the ulnar side of the palm, causing flexion contractures of the ring and little fingers.
De Quervain disease affects the first dorsal compartment, mostly in middle-aged women and around pregnancy. Its diagnostic test is Finkelstein's, not Phalen's.
LMN lesions cause flaccid tone, fasciculations and a flexor plantar with reduced or absent reflexes. Hyperreflexia is an UMN sign.
Dupuytren disease often shows autosomal dominant inheritance with variable penetrance and is linked to HIV and epilepsy. It mainly affects the ulnar side, not the radial side.
Heberden and Bouchard nodes indicate osteoarthritis, and boutonniere deformity is typical of RA. Swan-neck deformity is an RA deformity, not an OA one.
Compartment syndrome usually follows a fracture, and pain on passive stretch is early. Loss of pulses is a late sign, and Volkmann contracture is a late sequel.
CTEV comprises cavus, adductus, varus and equinus and is about twice as common in boys. It is scored with Pirani or Dimeglio and treated by Ponseti serial casting.
Ewing sarcoma is diaphyseal with onion-skin periosteal reaction and t(11;22); distal femoral metaphysis is the typical site of osteosarcoma.
Breast and lung are leading sources of spinal metastases. Lymphoma and prostate deposits are radiosensitive, but renal cell carcinoma is radioresistant.
Tinel, Phalen and Froment are correctly matched. Allen's test assesses both radial and ulnar artery supply, not the ulnar artery alone.
Untreated compartment syndrome can cause myoglobinuric renal failure, Volkmann contracture, gangrene and limb loss. AVN of the femoral head is not a sequel.
Perthes disease mainly affects boys and causes avascular necrosis with head collapse, and containment surgery is an option. Prognosis is better in younger, not older, children.
Young children all have flat feet, and about 15% of adults do. Painless flexible flat foot needs no treatment, and rigid flat foot suggests tarsal coalition.
Mallet toe is isolated DIP flexion with normal MTP and PIP joints. The claw toe and hammer toe descriptions are correct, so statement 3 is false.
The RA hand shows swan-neck and boutonniere deformities, MCP ulnar deviation with radial deviation at the wrist (zig-zag), and Vaughan-Jackson extensor tendon ruptures.
Frozen shoulder affects women in their fifties, is linked to diabetes and thyroid disease, and settles over 1-2 years. Radiographs are normal.
UMN lesions cause spasticity, an extensor plantar and a positive Hoffmann sign. Wasting is only mild disuse atrophy, less than in LMN lesions.
CTS is median nerve compression with night pain and late thenar wasting; symptoms are relieved by shaking the hand, not by wrist extension.
Palmar nodules, flexion contractures and Garrod's pads are features; Peyronie's disease is an associated fibromatosis, so statement 4 is false.
Ponseti correction follows CAVE: cavus first, then forefoot abduction that also corrects hindfoot varus, then equinus via Achilles tenotomy.
Eosinophilic granuloma is unifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis of skull and long bones causing vertebra plana; Letterer-Siwe is the disseminated multisystem form.
Cauda equina syndrome gives back pain, saddle anaesthesia, variable bladder symptoms and bilateral sciatica; confirmed cases need urgent surgical decompression.
With ageing, lumbar lordosis tends to decrease while thoracic kyphosis increases, so statement 4 is false. The stated normal ranges match common reference values.
Hallux valgus is lateral deviation at the first MTPJ, claw toe includes DIP flexion, and mallet toe is isolated DIP flexion. Hammer toe is defined by PIP flexion with the MTPJ essentially normal.
Ganglia are the commonest hand swellings, lie on the dorsal or volar wrist and transilluminate. Seed ganglia arise from the flexor sheath at the base of the finger.
Knee OA is commoner in women, with use-related pain and osteophytes; arthroplasty is for end-stage disease, not first line.
Adhesive capsulitis is capsular fibrosis and contraction without bony change, so plain radiographs are normal.
Compartment pressure kills tissue at levels well below systolic arterial pressure, so distal pulses persist and pulselessness comes late.
Dupuytren disease mainly affects men in their 5th-7th decades. Its inheritance is autosomal dominant with variable penetrance, not X-linked.
Ewing sarcoma gives a moth-eaten lesion with onion-skin reaction, but it arises in the diaphysis, not the epiphysis.
Confirmed cauda equina syndrome needs urgent decompression, ideally within 24-48 hours, because delay raises the risk of permanent sphincter and saddle deficits.
In Finkelstein test, ulnar deviation with the thumb clasped stretches APL and EPB and reproduces De Quervain pain, so R explains A.
Children presenting with Perthes disease at a younger age (under about 6 years) do better because more growth remains for the femoral head to remodel.
Lumbar flexion enlarges the canal and foramina, relieving neurogenic claudication of spinal stenosis.
Allen's test confirms adequate ulnar collateral flow through the palmar arch before the radial artery is harvested as a conduit.
Parosteal osteosarcoma has a long, mild course because it is a low-grade surface tumour, not a high-grade intramedullary one.
Mild Dupuytren's contracture with a palpable cord can be treated by percutaneous needle fasciotomy or collagenase. Severe contracture needs fasciectomy.
Under the Hueter-Volkmann principle, compression across the physis slows chondrocyte proliferation and longitudinal growth, while tension speeds it up.
Excising a Morton neuroma usually relieves pain, but a stump neuroma at the cut nerve end can cause recurrent pain.
Radial styloid pain in a new mother with a positive Finkelstein test is De Quervain tenosynovitis.
Once cavus, adductus and varus are corrected, Ponseti treatment corrects residual equinus by percutaneous Achilles tenotomy.
Bilateral calf pain on walking that is relieved by stooping forward is neurogenic claudication from lumbar canal stenosis.
A felon (pulp space abscess) needs prompt incision and drainage with antibiotics to prevent osteomyelitis of the terminal phalanx.
Perthes disease is managed by keeping hip movement (non-operative) or by containment surgery. Arthroplasty is not used in children.
Established acute compartment syndrome with raised pressure needs urgent fasciotomy as definitive treatment.
Severe Dupuytren's contracture is treated by surgical fasciectomy or release. Less invasive options suit milder disease.
Letterer-Siwe disease is the acute disseminated multisystem form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
A soft-tissue mass that is over 5 cm, deep to fascia, growing and painful carries a high risk of sarcoma and needs specialist assessment.
A painless, transilluminant dorsal wrist swelling that becomes more prominent on palmar flexion is a ganglion.
Idiopathic clubfoot is multifactorial with a familial tendency. Recurrence is higher when a parent is affected, but there is no single-gene Mendelian pattern.
Gamekeeper (skier) thumb is injury to the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb MCP joint.
Under the Hueter-Volkmann principle, tension across the physis stimulates growth and compression inhibits it.
A felon is an abscess within the closed fibrous septal compartments of the fingertip pulp.
Jefferson fracture is an axial-loading burst fracture of the atlas ring.
Peyronie disease is fibromatosis of the tunica albuginea, causing penile curvature. It is part of the Dupuytren diathesis.
Ledderhose disease is plantar fibromatosis, nodular thickening of the plantar fascia.
Sever disease is osteochondrosis (traction apophysitis) of the calcaneal apophysis.
Fasciotomy is indicated when diastolic pressure minus compartment pressure (delta P) is 30 mmHg or less.
Preiser disease is idiopathic avascular necrosis of the scaphoid.
Dupuytren disease is linked to smoking, alcohol, diabetes, epilepsy, HIV and, in some lists, hypothyroidism. Hyperthyroidism is not a recognised association.
Dupuytren's contracture is a palmar fascia disease of the hand and does not affect leg length.
Fasciculations come from denervation and are a lower motor neuron sign. Hyperreflexia, Babinski sign and clonus are UMN signs.
Mild De Quervain tenosynovitis is first managed with NSAIDs, a thumb spica splint and steroid injection. Surgical release of the first dorsal compartment is a last resort.
Pulses usually persist in early compartment syndrome. Disproportionate pain, pain on passive stretch and paraesthesia appear first.
Breast carcinoma is usually given as the commonest source of spinal metastases, followed by lung and prostate.
Phalen, Tinel, Froment (adductor pollicis, ulnar nerve) and Allen (radial and ulnar artery supply) are all correctly described.
Kienbock affects the lunate and Kohler the navicular. Panner affects the capitellum and Freiberg the second metatarsal head, so 3 and 4 are swapped.
Statements 1-3 are true; parosteal osteosarcoma is a low-grade surface tumour with a good prognosis.
Claw toe has MTP hyperextension, hammer toe a normal MTP, mallet toe isolated DIP flexion, and hallux valgus is angulation at the first MTP joint.
Parosteal osteosarcoma arises from the bone surface, typically the posterior distal femur, not the proximal humerus; most osteosarcomas are intramedullary.
Urgent MRI, saddle anaesthesia and bilateral sciatica are correct; decompression is advised as soon as possible rather than a 48-hour standard, though 48 h appears in older outcome data.
Chronic diseases are permanent, caused by non-reversible pathology, need long supervision and leave residual disability.
The Jai Vigyan RF/RHD project covers streptococcal sore throat epidemiology, RF/RHD registries, vaccine development and pathological studies, not mass treatment of all sore throats.
Metabolic syndrome includes hypertension, not hypotension, along with hyperglycaemia, hyperinsulinaemia and dyslipidaemia.
The mortality table needed to compute observed and expected deaths is missing from the stem; SMR = observed/expected x 100.
BCG is intradermal; hepatitis B, pentavalent and full-dose IPV are given intramuscularly.
Health education relies on actively acquired knowledge, appeals to reason and is behaviour-centred; appeals to emotion and arousing primitive desires characterise propaganda.
Role playing is a group method of health education; internet, direct mailing and posters are mass approaches.
Role play is a group approach; folk methods, posters and health exhibitions are mass approaches.
Preventing emergence of risk factors by preserving traditional healthy lifestyles is primordial prevention.
HDI uses life expectancy at birth, education (mean and expected years of schooling) and GNI per capita; infant mortality is not included.
PQLI combines infant mortality, life expectancy at age one and literacy; it excludes per capita income.
Normal karyotype as first requisite, role of genetic screening, and genetic potential becoming phenotypic reality in a healthy environment are all standard statements on biological determinants.
DALY = years of life lost to premature death plus years lived with disability.
Health care delivery indicators include doctor-population, doctor-nurse, population-bed ratios, population per subcentre and per trained birth attendant.
The Ottawa Charter's five action areas include healthy public policy, community action and reorienting health services.
PQLI consolidates infant mortality, literacy and life expectancy at age one.
The sequence is disease, impairment, disability, handicap.
Ideal health indicators should be valid, reliable, sensitive, specific, feasible and relevant.
Populations with different age compositions are compared using age-standardised death rates; the missing table does not change this.
The Weekly Epidemiological Record is a WHO publication; CD Alert is from NCDC India and MMWR from the US CDC.
The 'whole child' concept and country health programming approach is associated with UNICEF.
Egg protein is the reference protein for its high biological value, digestibility and complete essential amino acids; its caloric value is the same 4 kcal/g as other proteins.
Dietary fibre is not digested or absorbed as a nutrient and is described as having no metabolic effect.
Night blindness is the earliest symptom, but conjunctival xerosis is the first clinically visible sign of vitamin A deficiency.
Proline is non-essential; leucine, threonine and tryptophan are essential amino acids.
Fat per 100 g: buffalo about 6.5 g, goat about 4.5 g, cow about 4.1 g, human about 3.4 g.
Linoleic (PUFA) and oleic (MUFA) acids are unsaturated; lauric and palmitic acids are saturated.
Latent iron deficiency, with exhausted stores and transferrin saturation below 15% but no anaemia, is the most prevalent stage in India.
Proteins maintain oncotic pressure, support cell-mediated immunity and are needed for hormone synthesis; energy supply is not their key role.
Trans fatty acids are geometric isomers of cis fatty acids, persist in the body for years, are more atherogenic than saturated fats, and raise LDL while lowering HDL.
Serum ferritin reflects body iron stores and is the single most sensitive index of iron status.
By ICMR 2010, a sedentary woman needs about 1900 kcal/day plus about 600 kcal/day in the first 6 months of lactation, roughly 2500 kcal/day.
Menstrual iron loss is about 12.5 mg per 28-day cycle.
Neonatal hypothyroidism is the most sensitive indicator of environmental iodine deficiency.
Vitamin K1 (phylloquinone) comes mainly from green leafy vegetables; K2 is made by gut bacteria.
Endemic ascites is caused by pyrrolizidine alkaloids from Crotalaria seeds contaminating millet, a naturally occurring plant toxin.
The adult body contains about 25 g of magnesium, not 50 g; the other statements are true.
Median urinary iodine excretion reflects recent intake and is the main impact indicator of salt iodisation.
Neonatal tetanus elimination means fewer than 1 case per 1000 live births per year in every district.
Abacavir is an NRTI; amprenavir and indinavir are protease inhibitors and nevirapine is an NNRTI.
Pegloticase is PEG-conjugated recombinant uricase for refractory chronic gout; infusion reactions and anti-drug antibodies are its main problems.
Secukinumab targets IL-17A; ustekinumab targets IL-12/23 p40, while infliximab and etanercept block TNF.
Classic PAN affects medium arteries and spares glomeruli, causing renal infarcts rather than glomerulonephritis.
Sulfasalazine is the DMARD of choice for peripheral arthritis in ankylosing spondylitis.
A vocabulary of 8-10 words is expected around 15-18 months, not at 12 months, when 1-2 meaningful words are typical.
At 3-4 months an infant fixates intently, grasps with the eyes and has well-established binocular vision; following rapidly moving objects comes at about one year.
DQ = developmental age / chronological age x 100 = 2/4 x 100 = 50%.
ASQ-3 covers 1 to 66 months (5.5 years); the Trivandrum chart covers 0-2 years and Bayley up to about 42 months.
After day 5 of illness NS1 declines and IgM capture ELISA is the preferred diagnostic test for dengue.
Acute afebrile limp with restricted hip movement and normal X-ray in a young child is transient synovitis of the hip.
Salivation, lacrimation, miosis, cramps and emesis form the muscarinic cholinergic toxidrome of carbamate or organophosphate anticholinesterase poisoning.
Persistent allergic rhinitis is best treated with an intranasal corticosteroid such as fluticasone, the most effective single therapy.
Vomiting, diarrhoea and jaundice in the first week after milk feeds begin, together with early cataracts, are typical of classic galactosaemia (GALT deficiency).
At 3-4 months an infant fixates intently, grasps with the eyes and has well-established binocular vision; following rapidly moving objects comes at about one year.
A renal calculus is retroperitoneal and overlies the vertebral column on a lateral film, whereas gallstones lie anterior to it.
Ectopic ureters are commoner in females, usually drain the upper moiety of a duplex kidney, and can cause continuous incontinence.
RCC arises from proximal tubular epithelium, is commoner in males, has clear cell, papillary and chromophobe subtypes, and is treated surgically when localised.
ADPKD has hepatic, pancreatic and arachnoid cysts, renal and extrarenal features, faster progression in men, and usually presents after 30 years.
A 46,XX girl with normal ovaries and secondary sexual characters but absent uterus has Mullerian agenesis (MRKH).
AIS is X-linked recessive, 46,XY, with normal or raised male testosterone; Barr body is absent.
Primary amenorrhoea is no menses by 14 years without secondary sexual characters, or by 16 years with them.
Amenorrhoea after curettage with normal FSH, negative progesterone challenge and honeycomb HSG indicates intrauterine synechiae (Asherman syndrome).
PCOS metabolic syndrome criteria use waist circumference, triglycerides, HDL, blood pressure and fasting glucose, not BMI; the explanation labels the answer D but argues for BMI.
POI is ovarian failure before 40 with FSH above 40 on two tests 4 weeks apart and low estradiol.
HSG assesses the tubes, cervical incompetence and a translocated IUD; subserosal fibroids do not distort the cavity and are not shown.
HSG is done after menses stop and before ovulation, about days 6-10, to avoid spreading menstrual debris and irradiating an early pregnancy.
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is the commonest congenital cause of primary testicular failure, with eunuchoid habitus, azoospermia, gynaecomastia, low testosterone and high gonadotropins.
46,XY with female internal genitalia and bilateral streak gonads is complete gonadal dysgenesis (Swyer syndrome).
LDH is a marker of dysgerminoma, not of serous epithelial cancer, which is followed with CA-125 and HE4. The other pairings are correct.
Endometrial hyperplasia or malignancy must be excluded and contraindicates endometrial ablation.
The Gilliam procedure is a ventrosuspension for a retroverted uterus. Haultain, Spinelli and Kustner operations correct uterine inversion.
Pregnancy symptoms with amenorrhoea but no gestation, plus altered LH pulsatility and raised androgens, is pseudocyesis; the option letters inside the texts are scrambled.
In PCOS, hyperinsulinaemia and androgens suppress hepatic SHBG, so SHBG is low, not high.
Acute PID, suspected genital tuberculosis and active uterine bleeding contraindicate HSG; infertility is its main indication.
OHSS risk is higher with young age, PCOS, rapidly rising estradiol and many follicles (necklace sign); advanced age is protective.
The classic definition of secondary amenorrhoea is no menses for 6 months; newer definitions use 3 months if cycles were previously regular.
HAIR-AN stands for hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance and acanthosis nigricans.
Good asthma control means daytime symptoms and reliever use at most twice a week, rare night waking and minimal exacerbations; reliever use more than twice a week means poor control.
Silica, cadmium and coal dust are recognised occupational causes of COPD; asbestos mainly causes fibrosis, pleural disease and cancers.
With post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7, an FEV1 of 50-79% predicted is GOLD 2, moderate.
Chronic rhinosinusitis, recurrent chest infections, dextrocardia and immotile sperm indicate primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener syndrome).
A bronchus larger than its artery (signet ring) and tram-track lines on HRCT, with copious purulent sputum, indicate bronchiectasis.
Cystic fibrosis is confirmed by sweat chloride and CFTR mutation analysis, with faecal fat showing pancreatic insufficiency; lung biopsy is not used.
In the natural history of primary TB, haematogenous spread causing miliary TB and meningitis typically occurs about 3-6 months after infection.
CBNAAT detects rifampicin resistance, LPA detects isoniazid and rifampicin resistance, and LED fluorescence beats ZN; IGRA cannot diagnose active TB.
Isoniazid causes pyridoxine-deficiency peripheral neuropathy.
Ethambutol causes optic (retrobulbar) neuritis with red-green colour vision loss.
Asthma with brown mucus plugs, fleeting infiltrates and total IgE above 1000 points to allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis.
Hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy, SIADH, paraneoplastic nephrotic syndrome and hCG-related gynaecomastia are all non-metastatic manifestations of lung cancer.
Thymic tumours, retrosternal goitre, germ cell tumours and lymphoma are anterior mediastinal lesions. Neurogenic tumours are typically posterior.
Some standard sources call interstitial fibrosis the commonest pulmonary manifestation of RA, while others name pleural disease, so A and C are both defensible.
Extensive sclerosis of chest wall skin in systemic sclerosis restricts chest movement, called hidebound chest.
Penicillin, sulfasalazine, methotrexate and nadolol are listed among drugs causing pulmonary eosinophilia.
Pleural plaques are the most common manifestation of past asbestos exposure.
The classic threshold is mean PAP of 25 mmHg or more at rest; 2022 guidelines lowered it to above 20 mmHg.
Phrenic palsy, subphrenic abscess and lung volume loss after lobectomy raise a hemidiaphragm; pleural effusion does not truly elevate it.
Cheese washer's lung is hypersensitivity pneumonitis from mouldy cheese, attributed to Penicillium casei and Aspergillus clavatus.
Eggshell calcification of hilar nodes is classically seen in silicosis.
Obesity, acromegaly, male sex and alcohol all predispose to obstructive sleep apnoea.
In the proliferative phase of ARDS, type II pneumocytes proliferate to re-epithelialise the alveoli; hyaline membranes belong to the exudative phase.
Adequate PEEP prevents cyclic alveolar collapse and reopening, which is atelectrauma.
Under the Berlin definition, a PaO2/FiO2 of 100 mmHg or less with PEEP of at least 5 is severe ARDS.

Traumatic tamponade from a penetrating cardiac wound needs immediate operative decompression and repair. Pericardiocentesis is only a temporising bridge.
Traumatic tamponade needs surgical decompression because blood clots and the source must be repaired; a small volume causing compression is true but does not explain avoiding pericardiocentesis.

Base of skull fracture gives CSF otorrhoea, rhinorrhoea and Battle's sign; unilateral mydriasis with ptosis indicates third nerve compression.
The primary survey covers oxygenation and circulation, excluding hypoglycaemia and checking pupils; mechanism of injury belongs to the history and secondary survey.
Rising respiratory rate and pulse and falling blood pressure suggest ongoing bleeding; serum lactate rises, not falls.
A sucking chest wound arises when the chest wall defect is large enough (about two-thirds of the tracheal diameter, often quoted as over 3 cm) that air enters preferentially through it.
Diaphragmatic injuries are often silent, may show the NG tube in the chest, and are best evaluated by laparoscopy or VATS; acute repairs are usually done through the abdomen.
In neurotmesis the nerve is completely divided, sheath included, so recovery is poor without surgical repair.
In axonotmesis the axons are disrupted with Wallerian degeneration, but the sheath stays intact and regeneration usually happens without surgery.

The liver tolerates hepatic artery ligation because the portal vein carries most of its blood and oxygen, and that dual supply also explains why the portal vein must not be ligated. R seems to explain A.
In the Glasgow Coma Scale the maximum eye score is 4, verbal 5 and motor 6; an intubated patient's verbal score is recorded as T.
Extradural haematoma follows middle meningeal artery injury with squamous temporal fracture and is biconvex on CT; it usually needs urgent evacuation.
A liquefied chronic subdural haematoma is usually evacuated through burr holes with irrigation and drainage.
A chronic subdural haematoma is hypodense on CT and enlarges slowly as the degrading clot expands osmotically; acute SDH follows high-energy injury or minor trauma in anticoagulated elderly.
Neurapraxia is a conduction block with intact axons and sheath and no Wallerian degeneration, so it recovers spontaneously.
Serum amylase and lipase are neither sensitive nor specific for pancreatic injury; CT is the main test in blunt trauma and laparotomy finds it in penetrating trauma.
Damage control thresholds include temperature below 34 C, pH below 7.2, lactate above 5 mmol/L and systolic BP below 70 to 90 mmHg. Of the thresholds offered, only lactate above 5 is correct.
Unstable liver trauma needs laparotomy, the hepatic artery can be ligated while the portal vein is repaired or shunted, and closed drainage is used rather than open drainage.

Skull base fractures can cause pituitary dysfunction, cranial nerve palsies and carotid dissection; a CSF leak carries a meningitis risk.
Tamponade raises CVP, distends neck veins and lowers arterial pressure (Beck triad); tracheal deviation suggests tension pneumothorax.
Clamping a drain does not tamponade massive haemothorax bleeding; the shock, flat neck veins and dullness described are true but do not explain this.
Damage control thresholds include systolic BP below 70 mmHg, temperature below 34 C, pH below 7.2 and lactate above 5 mmol/L. The other options give the wrong cut-offs.
Diffuse axonal injury is primary brain injury from high-energy acceleration-deceleration; CT is often unremarkable and MRI is more sensitive.
Trauma is the most common cause of subarachnoid haemorrhage, but traumatic SAH is usually managed conservatively, not surgically.

eFAST cannot reliably exclude penetrating injury because it detects free fluid and misses organ or tract injury without haemoperitoneum.
Seat belt syndrome combines abdominal wall bruising with deceleration injuries; mesenteric tears are the commonest source of bleeding, not the liver.
FAST examines the abdomen; eFAST adds the pleural spaces and pericardium and detects roughly over 100 mL of free fluid, but is unreliable for hollow viscus injury.
Hypotension in head injury should prompt a search for blood loss elsewhere, because isolated head injury rarely causes hypotension except terminally.
Damage control surgery aims to prevent or break the lethal triad of hypothermia, acidosis and coagulopathy.
Stage II of damage control is the abbreviated operation to control haemorrhage and contamination, followed by temporary closure.

Early total care fixes all injuries definitively early, while damage control defers definitive surgery until physiology recovers. A switch to damage control mid-operation is allowed, and coagulopathy is an indication for it, not a bar.
Neurointensive care targets in head injury include PaO2 above 11 kPa, with PaCO2 of 4.5-5.0 kPa.
In cABCDE, c is catastrophic haemorrhage control, B breathing and ventilation, E exposure and environment; D stands for disability (neurological status).
Contrast whole-body CT is the standard imaging in severe blunt trauma because it assesses all regions at once and finds injuries missed clinically or by FAST.
The middle rectal artery arises from the internal iliac artery, not the external iliac.

The modern Calot triangle is bounded by the common hepatic duct medially, the liver's inferior surface above and the cystic duct and gallbladder laterally. Its key content is the cystic artery, though the right hepatic artery often crosses it.
OPSI risk is highest after splenectomy for haematological disease, not trauma; it peaks in the first 2-3 years, and vaccines are given at least 2 weeks before elective surgery.
Ventral hernias are anterior abdominal wall hernias (umbilical, epigastric, incisional, Spigelian, with lumbar included by convention). Groin hernias are excluded.
An infant with colicky screaming, drawn-up legs, an empty right iliac fossa and red currant jelly mucus has intussusception.
Ogilvie syndrome is colonic pseudo-obstruction with no mechanical cause; marked caecal dilatation, perforation risk and IV neostigmine treatment are typical.

GI neuroendocrine tumours arise from Kulchitsky (enterochromaffin) cells, secrete mainly serotonin and are followed with chromogranin A. The appendix has traditionally been quoted as the commonest site.
FAP means over 100 colorectal adenomas, usually with a family history, from an autosomal dominant APC mutation on chromosome 5q.
The classic MELD uses bilirubin, creatinine and INR; albumin is added only in the newer MELD 3.0.
Typhoid ulcers over Peyer patches lie along the long axis of the gut and perforate in the third week, most often in the terminal ileum.
A pseudocyst is drained endoscopically, percutaneously or surgically (cystogastrostomy). Pancreaticoduodenectomy is a resection for neoplasms.
Hepatic adenomas occur mainly in young women on oral contraceptives and are often incidental, but they can rupture and turn malignant.
Ectopic pancreas is classically found in the gastric/duodenal submucosa, within the liver and at the splenic hilum; the mesentery is a less standard site, making 1, 2 and 4 the intended answer.
Splenectomy is indicated for trauma, ITP and hypersplenism; pseudomyxoma peritonei is not an indication for splenectomy itself.
The Pringle manoeuvre clamps the hepatoduodenal ligament, which holds the portal triad: common bile duct, hepatic artery and portal vein. The IVC is not included.
Malnutrition, wound infection and immunosuppression impair fascial healing and predispose to incisional hernia. Slowly absorbable or non-absorbable sutures lower the risk.
Annular pancreas results from abnormal rotation of the ventral (not dorsal) bud; it encircles D2, causes duodenal obstruction and is treated by duodenoduodenostomy.
Ranson/Glasgow, APACHE II and modified Marshall scores grade acute pancreatitis; MELD is for chronic liver disease.
Retroperitoneal fibrosis is caused by drugs such as methysergide, lymphoma and carcinoid tumours; CAPD causes sclerosing encapsulating peritonitis instead.
Tokyo grade II (moderate) cholecystitis: WBC >18,000, palpable tender mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation; renal dysfunction denotes grade III.
Pyoderma gangrenosum and peripheral arthropathy parallel bowel activity while primary sclerosing cholangitis runs independently; the official key includes amyloidosis, which is debatable.
Achalasia is treated with botulinum toxin, pneumatic dilatation and Heller myotomy; beta blockers have no role.
Viable bowel shows peristalsis, a shiny serosa and mesenteric arterial pulsation; flabby, toneless muscle suggests non-viability.
Duodenal ulcers outnumber gastric ulcers, H. pylori and NSAIDs are the main causes, and posterior duodenal ulcers bleed from the gastroduodenal artery.
Ranson admission criteria are age >55, WBC >16,000, glucose >200 mg/dL, LDH >350 and AST >250; WBC >15,000 belongs to the Glasgow score.
Cystic fibrosis affects exocrine glands of the lungs, pancreas, liver and intestine; the kidney is not a typical target.
Lichtenstein, Stoppa and TEP are mesh-based tension-free repairs. Desarda is a tissue repair using an external oblique strip, though its proponents also call it tension-free.
Felty syndrome is rheumatoid arthritis with splenomegaly and neutropenia; splenectomy improves the blood picture only transiently in some.
A trichobezoar is a gastric hairball, usually in young women with trichotillomania or trichophagia. It can bleed, perforate or obstruct and needs removal, not PPIs.
Meckel's diverticulum is a true diverticulum (all coats) from the vitellointestinal duct, on the antimesenteric ileal border, with heterotopic mucosa in about 20 percent.
Left-sided colorectal cancers bleed and obstruct, right-sided ones cause iron deficiency anaemia, and colonoscopy is the investigation of choice. Left-sided tumours are more common.
FAP is autosomal dominant (statement 2 false); APC on 5q, near 100% colorectal cancer risk and CHRPE in a large share of cases are correct.
Fever with toxaemia a few days after peritonitis surgery, with shoulder tip pain and hiccups from diaphragmatic irritation, indicates a subphrenic abscess.
Barrett's oesophagus is columnar metaplasia from reflux, predisposes to adenocarcinoma and dysplasia can be treated by endoscopic resection; NSAIDs are not the cause.
Pseudocyst and acute fluid collection are local complications, and pleural effusion is listed among local complications in surgical classifications, while ileus is treated as systemic.
Smoking, diabetes and male sex raise pancreatic cancer risk; incidence is higher in Black rather than Caucasian populations.
Adult umbilical hernia occurs in obese patients with an attenuated raphe, causes pain from tissue tension and is classically repaired by Mayo's technique; women are affected more than men.
Morgagni hernia is a congenital anterior defect between sternal and costal diaphragmatic slips, usually containing omentum or transverse colon; it is anterior, not posterior.
Budd-Chiari mostly presents with abdominal discomfort and ascites; the caudate lobe (segment 1) hypertrophies and young women are mainly affected.
Splenic artery aneurysm is commoner in women, usually single and located in the main arterial trunk.
Late dumping is reactive hypoglycaemia in the second hour after a meal, lasting about 30-40 min with tremor, faintness and prostration; it is relieved by food, not lying down.
A screening test must be sensitive, specific and acceptable, and the disease should be detectable early; the disease should be common and important, not uncommon.
Plummer-Vinson syndrome is web, iron deficiency and dysphagia in middle-aged women with postcricoid cancer risk; treatment is iron and dilatation, not surgery.
Dengue has four serotypes, each giving lifelong homotypic immunity, and secondary infection especially with DENV-2 predisposes to severe dengue.
Aedes becomes infective after 8-10 days and stays infective for life; its genital tract does get infected, allowing transovarian transmission.
KFD is tick-borne and was first recognised in Karnataka, but was called monkey disease, not pig disease.
Monkeypox is an orthopoxvirus, an enveloped double-stranded DNA virus.
Central obesity drives insulin resistance, which explains why waist measures predict type 2 diabetes better than BMI.
Certificate validity became lifelong and applies to all certificates; validity starts 10 days after vaccination and no booster is needed.
Mantoux uses 1 TU PPD in 0.1 mL intradermally with a tuberculin syringe, bevel facing upward, raising a 6-10 mm wheal; so only statements 1 and 4 are correct.
Smoking raises BP via nicotine, promotes atherogenesis via carbon monoxide and lowers HDL; it does not reduce apolipoprotein B.
Diabetes screening targets people over 40, those with family history and women who delivered babies over 4.5 kg.
The 2025 End TB milestone is a 75% reduction in TB deaths versus 2015, so statement 3 is wrong; the others are correct.
Orchitis is the commonest extra-salivary manifestation of mumps in post-pubertal males.
Smoking, obesity and sedentary habits are modifiable CHD risk factors; age is non-modifiable.
STDs are transmitted predominantly by direct sexual contact.
Measles is most infectious in the prodrome and infectivity falls after the rash. The secondary attack rate is high (about 90%), and one attack gives lifelong immunity, so only statement 2 is true.
Stavudine was phased out of first-line ART because of lipoatrophy, peripheral neuropathy and lactic acidosis.
Only monovalent hepatitis B vaccine is used for the birth dose.
Diphtheria incubation is 2-6 days; antitoxin is used for treatment and pentavalent vaccine includes diphtheria.
Syndrome X links insulin resistance with type 2 diabetes, hyperinsulinaemia, dyslipidaemia and hypertension, not hypercalcaemia.
DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) is a dietary plan for blood pressure control.
Covaxin is a whole-virion inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine.
Salt reduction, weight control and higher potassium intake all lower blood pressure.
Pentavalent vaccine covers diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Hib.
RIG is not recommended after day 7 from the first vaccine dose, because an active antibody response has begun. 'Till 15 days' is false.
Bedaquiline is a bactericidal diarylquinoline inhibiting mycobacterial ATP synthase, with a very long half-life and large tissue distribution.
Classical rabies is caused by Lyssavirus genotype/serotype 1.
The DASH diet is advocated for hypertension control.
The malaria strategy 2030 targets are 90% reduction in mortality and incidence versus 2015 and elimination in at least 35 countries.
GAPPD 2025 targets a 75% (not 90%) reduction in severe pneumonia incidence, alongside the mortality goals of <3 and <1 per 1000 live births.
The physical activity target is a 10% reduction, so B is incorrect, but the salt target is a 30% reduction, so C is also incorrect; two options fit NOT correct.
Symptomatic HIV infection contraindicates live BCG; low birth weight, prematurity and maternal TB do not.
ILRs are top-opening with two temperature zones, the lower part being colder; vaccines must not be placed directly on the floor.
The open vial policy covers DPT, TT, hepatitis B, OPV, pentavalent, PCV and IPV, not reconstituted BCG or measles vaccines.
Holoendemic describes high infection beginning early in childhood with less evident disease in adults, as in malaria.
Schistosomiasis follows a man-snail-man transmission chain.
Incidence counts only new cases in a defined population over a specified time, with the time unit stated; new plus old cases is prevalence.
Rare BCG reactions are suppurative lymphadenitis, osteitis and disseminated BCG infection; Guillain-Barre is not a recognised BCG reaction.
The diseases classically notifiable to WHO under the International Health Regulations were cholera, plague and yellow fever.
An ideal disinfectant is broad spectrum, fast acting and non-toxic.
An infected food handler repeatedly contaminating food gives a common-source continuous exposure epidemic.
Malaria is vector-borne (Anopheles) and does not spread by contact. Scabies, trachoma and leprosy spread through contact.
Hold-over time depends on ambient temperature, load, lid opening and ice-lining condition, not on the type of vaccine stored.
Influenza and chickenpox spread by droplet nuclei, and Q fever and psittacosis by infected dust, all forms of airborne transmission.

Non-randomised designs include uncontrolled trials, natural experiments and before-after studies; risk factor trials are randomised controlled trials.

Carriers of avirulent organisms are termed pseudo-carriers.

Obstetric haemorrhage is the leading cause of maternal deaths in India.
Raised maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein is a screening marker for open neural tube defects.
Respiratory infections, diarrhoea and congenital anomalies are principal causes of infant death; childhood cancers are not.
IMR = 200/2500 live births x 1000 = 80, well above India's national IMR of under 30; the denominator is live births and the numerator infant deaths.
In the older national ARI schedule, children of 10-19 kg received three paediatric cotrimoxazole tablets twice daily; current guidelines prefer amoxicillin.

A cystic hygroma (lymphatic malformation) appears in neonates as a soft, compressible neck swelling that transilluminates brilliantly and enlarges on crying.

Nasopharyngeal carcinoma is strongly associated with Epstein-Barr virus, is commoner in males and adults, and is treated mainly with radiotherapy.
POSSUM stands for Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and morbidity; it uses physiological and operative variables only.
Suxamethonium has the fastest onset and short action with spontaneous recovery as plasma cholinesterase hydrolyses it.
In Indian teaching, antepartum haemorrhage is genital tract bleeding after 28 weeks of pregnancy and before birth of the baby.
Advanced maternal age, smoking and previous caesarean scar predispose to placenta praevia; maternal anaemia does not.
Abruption causes uterine tenderness, hypertonus, fetal distress and preterm labour; labour tends to be rapid rather than prolonged.
Beta-thalassaemia trait shows raised HbA2 (>3.5%) with low MCV and usually normal MCHC and iron studies.
Hydroxychloroquine is safe in pregnancy and should be continued as maintenance therapy for SLE.

Peripartum cardiomyopathy typically affects multiparous women with LVEF below 45% and no prior heart disease; ACE inhibitors are avoided antenatally but used postpartum.
Iron deficiency anaemia in pregnancy shows Hb <10 g/dL, PCV <30% and a microcytic hypochromic smear, with MCHC below 30%.
Intrapartum zidovudine, elective caesarean when viral load is not suppressed and neonatal ARV prophylaxis reduce transmission; amniotomy and oxytocin augmentation are avoided.
Obstetric cholestasis causes third-trimester palmoplantar pruritus with raised bile acids, resolving after delivery; bilirubin rarely exceeds 5 mg/dL.
Iron deficiency shows low serum iron, transferrin saturation 10% or less and ferritin below 30; TIBC is raised above 400 microgram/dL.
Intrapartum penicillin G is the first-line agent for GBS prophylaxis/treatment in pregnancy.
Opioids (histamine release), PGF2-alpha and ergometrine can provoke bronchospasm; PGE1 (misoprostol) is safe in asthma.
Malaria in pregnancy causes thrombocytopenia, hypoglycaemia and DIC; it produces metabolic acidosis, not alkalosis.
Iron transfer to the fetus is largely maintained, so the fetus is not severely anaemic even if the mother is.
A uniformly enlarged, boggy, tender uterus with progressive dysmenorrhea and menorrhagia in a multiparous woman in her late thirties is classic adenomyosis.
An irregularly enlarged uterus with heavy menstrual bleeding and a negative pregnancy test points to leiomyoma; adenomyosis gives a uniform enlargement.
Submucous fibroids are the least common type (about 5%) but distort the cavity and are most strongly linked to infertility and miscarriage.
Red degeneration occurs mainly in pregnancy and the puerperium, is vascular rather than infective, shows a raw-beef cut surface, and partial recovery is called necrobiosis.
Mature cystic teratoma (dermoid) is the most common ovarian neoplasm found in pregnancy.
Placental site trophoblastic tumour is made of intermediate trophoblast, so hCG is low and hPL high, and it invades the myometrium.
Sheets of anaplastic cyto- and syncytiotrophoblast with no chorionic villi define choriocarcinoma; invasive mole keeps villi.
Mucinous cystadenoma is a surface epithelial tumour, so statement I is false; the correct set II, III and IV is not offered, and options C and D are identical.
Progestogen from the LNG-IUS opposes estrogen in the endometrium and protects against hyperplasia; tamoxifen, nulliparity and obesity raise the risk.
Endometriosis is ectopic functioning endometrium, depends on estrogen, commonly involves the ovary, and is diagnosed by laparoscopy as the gold standard.
Adenomyosis is endometrium within myometrium, gives a uniformly enlarged boggy uterus and can mimic fibroid; it presents with menorrhagia and dysmenorrhea, not primary amenorrhea.
Sarcoma botryoides is an embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma of infants and young girls with grape-like vaginal masses; it is malignant and needs multimodal treatment.
Dysgerminoma is the commonest malignant ovarian germ cell tumour, can be bilateral and allows fertility-sparing surgery; it is highly radio- and chemosensitive.
Smoking lowers estrogen exposure and is associated with fewer fibroids; early menarche, nulliparity and obesity increase risk.
Postmenopausal status, abnormal bleeding and larger polyp size predict malignant change in endometrial polyps; multiplicity is not an established predictor.
Red degeneration is a vascular change of pregnancy and puerperium with a raw-beef cut surface and possible partial recovery (necrobiosis); infection plays no part.
Primary dysmenorrhea occurs in adolescents with ovulatory cycles, often eases after vaginal delivery, and by definition has no pelvic pathology.
In POP-Q the hymen is zero, points above it are negative and below it positive, and total vaginal length is measured with the prolapse reduced; so only 1 and 4 are correct.
A cystocele is reducible, shows an impulse on coughing and admits a metal catheter into the bulge; a Gartner cyst has none of these and has defined margins.
The current WHO lower reference limits are volume 1.4 mL, total motility 42%, progressive motility 30% and normal morphology 4%, so all four are listed values.
A simple vesicovaginal fistula is small, supratrigonal, and occurs without malignancy or prior radiation; prior radiation makes a fistula complex.

In the three-swab test with dye in the bladder, dye staining the middle swab indicates a vesicovaginal fistula; urine-wet but unstained swabs suggest a ureteric fistula and a stained lower swab a urethral one.
Hegar sign is the soft isthmus allowing abdominal and vaginal fingers to appose below the uterine body on bimanual examination at 6 to 10 weeks.
In sickle cell pregnancy, iron is given only for proven deficiency, hydroxyurea is stopped before conception, penicillin prophylaxis is advised and unpressurised air travel is avoided.
Ruptured membranes, a dead fetus and previous caesarean are listed contraindications to external cephalic version, and obesity is listed in standard Indian teaching as one too.
Hyperemesis can cause peripheral neuritis and Wernicke encephalopathy, Mallory-Weiss tears, and convulsions or coma; cardiac failure is not a recognised complication.
Occipitoposterior position is favoured by anthropoid or android pelvis, high pelvic inclination, anterior placenta and abnormal uterine contractions; gynecoid pelvis and posterior placenta do not.
Hydramnios, twins, prematurity and stabilising induction with low rupture of membranes all predispose to cord prolapse.
The first-trimester scan in twins confirms the number, viability and chorionicity, and screens for major malformations.
Painful bleeding with a tense, tender uterus and absent fetal heart at 34 weeks with a closed os is typical of concealed or mixed abruptio placentae.
Third-trimester pruritus of palms and soles without rash, with raised bile acids and mildly raised transaminases, is intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy.
Fetal meconium appears around the 20th week; breathing movements start near 11 weeks, surfactant around 24 weeks and insulin secretion near 12 weeks.
In pregnancy, maternal serum iodine falls from increased renal clearance, while CRH, ACTH and aldosterone all rise.
A head that is incompletely flexed engages with the suboccipitofrontal diameter (10 cm); full flexion uses suboccipitobregmatic and deflexion occipitofrontal.
Normal pregnancy is diabetogenic: insulin resistance with raised insulin secretion gives fasting hypoglycaemia and postprandial hyperglycaemia.

The plane of least pelvic dimensions is the narrowest plane, starts the forward curve of the pelvic axis and marks the ischial spines for pudendal block; internal, not external, rotation occurs there.
In pregnancy cardiac output, stroke volume and heart rate rise while systemic vascular resistance falls, so only 1 and 3 are correct.
hCG is a placental glycoprotein whose alpha subunit is shared with LH, FSH and TSH; its levels are higher, not lower, in multiple pregnancy.
Amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea, headache and visual field loss with prolactin above 100 ng/mL indicate a prolactin-secreting pituitary macroadenoma.
A 46,XY phenotypic female with breasts, scanty pubic and axillary hair, blind vagina, absent uterus and male testosterone has complete androgen insensitivity.
Normal stature, female genitalia and bilateral streak gonads define pure gonadal dysgenesis; Swyer syndrome is its 46,XY form, and no karyotype is given, so the general term fits best.
Postpartum blues start in the first week, affect about half of mothers and settle with reassurance; no specific endocrine abnormality has been shown.
Placenta accreta results pathologically from absent decidua basalis and a deficient Nitabuch layer; loss of the retroplacental clear zone is an ultrasound sign, not a pathological finding.
Coliforms are excreted in huge numbers and easily cultured, and they survive longer and resist natural purification better than pathogens, so only I and IV are correct.
The housefly carries organisms on its legs, body hairs, vomit drops and faeces, so it transmits disease mainly mechanically.
The recommended illumination for general office work is about 400 lux.
Composting, as in the Bangalore method, is the combined disposal of refuse and night soil or sludge.
Septic tanks suit single houses or small groups, need an air space of about 30 cm under the cover, and their effluent still carries pathogens, so all three statements are wrong.
Sewage treatment runs from screening to grit chamber to primary sedimentation, and later the sludge goes to the digester.
Studies show an inverse statistical association: areas with softer water have higher cardiovascular death rates.
Caisson disease (decompression sickness) affects divers and workers in pressurised caissons and tunnels below sea or water level when they decompress rapidly.
Cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive and Huntington chorea autosomal dominant, but Marfan syndrome is autosomal dominant, not sex-linked recessive, so two pairs are correct.
Haemophilia is an inherited X-linked bleeding disorder with equal incidence across ethnic groups; carrier females are only occasionally and mildly affected.
Maple syrup urine disease is a classic inborn error of amino acid metabolism; Tay-Sachs, a lysosomal enzyme defect, is technically one too, but B is the intended answer.
Amniocentesis is indicated for maternal age 35 or more, a previous chromosomal anomaly or a parental translocation; advanced paternal age is not a listed indication.
The nuclear family life cycle runs through formation, extension, contraction and dissolution.

An undescended testis stops along its normal path, most often within the inguinal canal; the superficial inguinal pouch is the commonest site of an ectopic testis.
Undescended testis carries higher risks of infertility, malignancy, torsion and an associated inguinal hernia.
Varicocele is mostly left sided, feels like a bag of worms, decompresses on lying down, and microsurgical varicocelectomy has the best results with fewest complications.
